newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PLAY SET TO BEGIN AT WIMBLEDON, EARLY START ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PLAY SET TO BEGIN AT WIMBLEDON, EARLY START ON THURSDAY.

text.p: Play at Wimbledon on the third day on Wednesday, severely curtailed by rain, was finally set to go ahead on the main courts at 1800 local (1700GMT).

Drizzle continued for much of the afternoon, but soon after 1730 local (1630GMT), the covers were rolled back on Centre Court, although there was no prospect of play until at least 1800 local (1700GMT) on the outside courts.
Patient fans on Centre Court, who had kept up their spirits with a Mexican Wave, under umbrellas, looked like being rewarded, although clouds still hovered around.
Weather permitting, play on outside courts on Thursday will start an hour earlier than usual at 1000GMT. Play on Centre and Number One Court will begin at 1100GMT, two hours ahead of the normal time.
Showers permitted only 16 matches to be completed on Monday's opening day, but there was a full day's play on Tuesday.

In 1992, the second Friday of Wimbledon was washed out, forcing the tournament to be extended into the Monday of the following week, but the wettest championships in recent memory were in 1991 when play took place on the middle Sunday for the first time.
Play was also extended into a third week last year when the women's and mixed doubles finals were delayed until the Monday.
